name: Gang of Four
hook: Turned Marxist theory and dub-reggae bass into art-school punk-funk, and named themselves after a Chinese Communist Party faction.
blurb: Formed by art students in Leeds, Gang of Four combined punk's aggression with funk rhythm and dub reggae's bass-heavy sound: Andy Gill's scraping guitar that never took solos, over Dave Allen's bass. Their lyrics were full of Marxist and Situationist political and economic ideas rather than typical rock subjects, in a genre that mostly avoided direct political language. Their 1979 album 'Entertainment!' is treated as a founding record of this "punk funk", and is cited as an influence by acts from R.E.M. to later dance-punk bands.

signatureTracks.title: Damaged Goods
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The template: jagged, non-melodic guitar, a dub-heavy bassline, and lyrics treating a relationship in the language of a commercial transaction.

signatureTracks.title: At Home He's a Tourist
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Pulled from a Top of the Pops performance over a lyric about condoms, a useful snapshot of how far the band's directness went.
